idea-plugin.name: Device Lab Veyra
idea-plugin.description:
Test your Android app the way your users really use it, in one click.

Device Lab Veyra is a control panel for your phone or emulator, right inside Android Studio. Switch to dark theme, the largest font, Arabic, right-to-left, slow animations or airplane mode instantly, and see how your app copes. No digging through Settings, no Developer options, no adb commands to remember.

One click, any condition

  • Theme: light, dark or auto.
  • Font size up to 200 % (Android 14+) and display size from Small to Largest: find text that gets cut off.
  • App language (Android 13+): Arabic, Hebrew, German, Finnish, Thai, Japanese, Hindi and more, plus Android's pseudolocales for spotting text you forgot to translate. Only your app changes; the phone keeps its language.
  • Right-to-left layout: your app restarts in RTL straight away.
  • Animations off, faster or up to 10× slower, layout bounds and show taps.
  • Airplane mode: see how your app behaves offline.
  • Clean status bar for store screenshots: 12:00, full battery, full signal, no notifications.

Presets

  • Worst case: largest font, largest display size, right-to-left and dark theme at once. The hardest screen your layout will ever meet, in one click.
  • Screenshot ready, Slow motion, and Reset, which puts the device back exactly as it was.

Your app

  • Finds your app's package name in build.gradle by itself.
  • Permissions: grant or revoke each runtime permission with a checkbox, to test "permission denied" paths.
  • Deep links: lists every link in your AndroidManifest.xml and Navigation graphs; open any of them on the device and see how long the screen took.
  • Restart app, Clear data (asks first) and Screenshot, which opens the picture in the editor.

Works with emulators and real phones (USB or Wi-Fi debugging), Android 8 and newer, in Android Studio and IntelliJ IDEA. It finds adb in your Android SDK by itself. Nothing leaves your computer: no account, no telemetry.

Open it from View → Tool Windows → Device Lab or Tools → Open Device Lab.
Made by FlightCoders, the team behind Veyra Studio.
